FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 438
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative David Faulkner
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 02/24/2026
House Bill 438 as introduced would reinstate the income tax refund check-off program for the
Victims of Crime and Leniency, Inc. which would increase the administrative obligations of the
Department of Revenue by an undetermined amount but would be offset by the allowed cost of
collection of up to 5% of the amount donated to the organization, as provided by current law.
The average annual contributions to the eighteen check-off programs in tax year 2024 was
approximately $10,607. The highest and lowest amounts received by the various check-off
recipients in tax year 2024, was $21,188 and $3,540, respectively.
